fallback chain (`feeCcy -> ccy -> getBotFeeUnit`).

fields.name: fill_price_display
fields.doc:
Average fill price. Native:
`spot_makePriceConvertor(...).toQuoteFormated(avgPx).round.toLocalizedString()`
— HALF_UP at the charge currency's `priceDig`.

fields.name: fill_price_unit
fields.doc:
Unit for the fill-price row title. Native: `chargeConvertor.quoteSymbol`,
i.e. the charge currency's `displayName` **accessor**, which falls back
to `ccyName` — `OKTChargeCurrency.m:24-30` returns `_displayName` only
when non-empty. The resolver matches that:
`history_displays::charge_currency_unit_and_dig` walks
`first_non_empty(&[display_name, ccy_name])`, same as the detail page's
`charge_unit` twin. The fallback is required, not incidental — the raw
`display_name` override is empty on every non-EEA charge currency, and
reading it bare rendered "Fill price (--)" where native showed
"Fill price (USDT)". Blank only when the charge currency itself does not
resolve; the Swift row then renders native's `emptyDefaultString`.

fields.name: total_turnover_display
fields.doc:
Total turnover = `accFillSz × avgPx`. Native:
`spot_makeQuoteCcyConvertor(...).targetFormatter(product).down.toLocalizedString()`
— **truncated** (toward zero) at the index config's `quoteDig`.

fields.name: total_turnover_unit
fields.doc:
Unit for the turnover row title. Native: `quoteConvertor.targetUnit`,
which is `tradeQuoteCcy` when the wire supplies it, else the
instrument's `displayQuoteCcy`.

fields.name: filled_amount_display
fields.doc:
Accumulated filled size. Native:
`spot_makeBaseCcyConvertor(...).toTargetFormatted(accFillSz).round.toLocalizedString()`
— HALF_UP at the index config's `baseDig`. (`toTargetNumber` is the
identity for spot, so no unit conversion precedes the format.)

fields.name: filled_amount_unit
fields.doc:
Unit for the filled-amount row title. Native:
`tradeConvertor.targetUnit` = the instrument's `displayBaseCcy`.

fields.name: fee_display
fields.doc:
Fee. Native:
`spot_makeConfigurableFeeConvertor(...).convert(fee).round.toLocalizedString()`
— HALF_UP at `feeDig` when the fee is charged in the base currency, else
at `quoteFeeDig`.

fields.name: inst_title
fields.doc:
The row's instrument title (e.g. `"BTC/USDT"`).

Twinned rather than left as a per-cell native call, because for **SPOT**
the whole chain is a pure function of instrument metadata + this wire row:
`displayInstId(...)` picks the first non-empty of
`instrument.displayId` → wire `displayId` → `instrument.instId` → wire
`instId`, and `instTitleWithBizType:` then does a bare
`stringByReplacingOccurrencesOfString:@"-" withString:@"/"`
(`NSString+OKTInstrument.m:37-39`). The g11n in that method only lives in
the SWAP / FUTURES branches, which Recurring Buy never reaches.

Blank when neither id resolves; the Swift row then renders native's
`emptyDefaultString`.

fields.name: fee_unit
fields.doc:
Unit for the fee row title. Native: `feeConvertor.symbol`. Blank whenever
the wire `feeCcy` is blank, because native's factory guards on
`okts_spot_feeCcy()` (`feeCcy?.nilIfEmpty`) and returns a **nil
convertor** — which blanks the fee VALUE too, not just the unit.

fields.doc:
VIP level string from the strategy-config response. The prior seam
hardcoded this to `"0"` natively rather than reading the real value —

fields.name: settle_ccy
fields.doc:
`settleCcy` query param for the strategy-config fetch. `None` omits the key, preserving
today's iOS wire (iOS never calls [`set_settle_ccy`](SmartArbitragePlaceOrderActions
::set_settle_ccy)). Android calls `set_settle_ccy` with the standalone
[`resolve_smart_arb_usd_settle_ccy`] reader (same underlying source this Record's own
`resolve_identity` populates its `settle_ccy` local from) rather than a native
`TradeCoreManager` read — kept as an explicit action param, not derived internally, so
the call can happen before/without a `resolve_identity` round-trip.

fields.name: coin_names
fields.doc:
`coinNames` query param for the strategy-config fetch. Android's
native `ccys` is always `""` for smart-arbitrage (no `setCcys` call on
this path), so Android calls
[`set_coin_names`](SmartArbitragePlaceOrderActions::set_coin_names)
with `""`; iOS never calls it and the key stays omitted.

fields.doc:

resolved (blank id, cold store, unknown instrument), same convention as `base_ccy`.

fields.name: display_base_ccy

fields.name: display_spot_trade_symbol

fields.name: investment_precision
fields.doc:
Investment/leverage-principal input decimal precision, mirroring native's
`getBiz(SWAP).getIndexConfig(inst_family)?.marginDig` via `OkBizTrait
::get_margin_dig_with_index`. Falls back to `DEFAULT_INVESTMENT_PRECISION` (mirrors
native's own `DEFAULT_MARGIN_DIGIT` fallback) when unresolved. `0` only before the first
`resolve_identity` completes — never a real precision value, so callers gate on `> 0`.

fields.name: route_asset_type_hint
fields.doc:
Raw `asset_type` hint from the last `resolve_identity` call, kept only so
`retry_identity_resolution` can retry with the exact original route.

fields.name: identity_fatal_error

Fatal, retryable `core_trading` resolution failure. Only ever set by `resolve_identity` /

fields.name: investment_validity
fields.doc:
`Option<…>` + `#[uniffi(default = None)]`, NOT a bare `#[uniffi(default)]`: this is an
enum-typed field, and a bare default on an enum-typed field only compiles under cargo —
bindgen `bail!`s on it (`uniffi_bindgen/src/bindings/swift/gen_swift/enum_.rs`; UniFFI
`DefaultValue::parse` only accepts `None`/`Some(...)`/`[]`/a `syn::Lit`, never a path like
`SmartArbitrageInvestmentValidity::Pristine`). `None` means "not yet computed" — distinct
from `Pristine` (computed, and the amount is untouched); `recompute_typed_validity` always
writes `Some(_)`. See `display` below for the same enum-field constraint on a `Record`.

fields.name: is_over_available_balance

name: adopt_quote_ccy
doc:
Adopt `quote_ccy`, switching to a supported currency when it is not
one recurring buy accepts.

Also the single writer of the snack-bar notice, which now covers TWO
events: a rejected currency being overridden, and the pair's quote
currency simply changing to another accepted one. Page entry and a
pay-with switch announce nothing — see `adopted_quote_ccy`.

Returns nothing; the outcome is in state. `trade_quote_ccy` holds
whatever was actually adopted, and `quote_ccy_switch_notice` holds
the currency switched to when a switch happened. The adopted value is
published to the shared channel so the recommendation tab sees it.

name: create_chrome
doc:
Shared host-chrome projection for `BotPlaceOrderActivity` /
`BotPlaceOrderChromeBinder`; mirrors
`SpotGridPlaceOrderInteractor::create_chrome` (the reference impl —
see `BotCreateChrome`'s own doc comment for the field contract).

Field sourcing:
- `pair_label`: the resolved SWAP/FUTURES route from the (never-
resolving) instrument-context cache peek, fed into the same
`format_trade_title` port Spot Grid uses. Absent (empty
`CTTradeTitle`) while the instrument context is cold — mirrors
`create_order`'s own `missing_instrument_context` gate rather than
guessing SWAP.
- `ticker`: `last_px` (the self-fed `InstTickerCallback` value
already used for order-pricing bounds), formatted at the resolved
convertor's price precision; `tone` tracks direction via
`last_px_tone` (`apply_last_px_tone`), the same algorithm as Spot
Grid's `market_price_tone`. Both require a resolved instrument
context — a cold context hides the ticker rather than showing an
unprecisioned number.
- `toolbar_more_visible`: `true` — the same provisional literal Spot
Grid's shared-host overflow entry uses today (pending per-bot
journey-completeness gating; see
`SpotGridCreatePresentation::toolbar_more_visible`'s doc comment).
- `toolbar_strategy_switch_enabled`: always `false` — Contract DCA
has no strategy-selector catalog (no such field exists on
`ContractDcaPlaceOrderState`), so switching strategies from this
screen is never offered. A real, sourced "no", not a stand-in for
missing data.

fields.name: trade_quote_ccy

readers address fields by name, and any positional construction keeps
compiling unchanged.

client that has not adopted `hint_text` degrades to today's bare number — a

`SmartArbitrageActionKind`, not a reuse of it** — they are 1:1 today, but `kind` is
identity (which action this is) and `label` is a presentation choice (what caption it
shows). Keeping them separate leaves room for the same `kind` to carry a different
`label` under some future capability without a breaking enum change; collapsing them

string resource via an exhaustive `when`/`match` — see `SmartArbitrageActionResources`
on the Kotlin side — so an unmapped variant is a compile error, not a silent drop.

**Deliberately carries only the four live variants — no reserved
`EventHistory`/`Pin`/`Unpin`/`Share`, unlike `Kind`/`Icon`/`JourneyKind` above.** The
reason to pre-declare a reserved variant there is that `Kind` is identity the catalog may
need to express before its journey is wired; that reasoning inverts for a label. A label
has no meaning until its action ships, and copy is a product/review decision, not
something this derivation can default. Pre-declaring a reserved label here would force a
guessed string into an exhaustive `when` today, with no reviewer in that loop — exactly
the risk that produced the missing-Reduce-positions defect this catalog's amendments
document. Adding a real `EventHistory`/`Pin`/`Unpin`/`Share` label later must break the
native `when` so its copy is chosen deliberately; that forced break is the point, not a
cost to avoid.

to a `BotDisplayText`, byte-identical to legacy
`getBotPnl(instId, instType, pnl = value, mSymbol = ccy, investmentUnit = …,
isShowUnit = true, minDigit = min_digit)` (StrategyConvert.kt:219-274) for the
**value portion** (the unit suffix stays native — see the module note).

Because the action-profit call sites pass `isShowSymbol` = its default
`false`, there is NO leading "+" on positives and NO color. The value path:
* precision = `max(profit_digit, coin_size_digit)` (legacy `getBotPrecision`)
* rounding = DOWN for `> 0`, UP for `<= 0`
* sign = AUTO (no "+"; negatives carry the inherent "-")
* `min_digit` is the legacy `getBotPnl(minDigit = …)` floor (the action-profit
rows pass `MIN_PRECISION = 2`); native pads to that many decimals.

Empty `value` → `Placeholder` ("--"); non-numeric → `Raw`. Delegates to the
existing `pnl_bot_display_direct(show_symbol = false)` leaf — the same leaf the
grid Parameter share-amount uses — so the math is shared and unit-tested.

`min_digit` is `u8` (matches `BotDisplayText::Number.min_digit`); the native
caller passes the legacy `MIN_PRECISION = 2`.

name: OKTSFFIErrorValue
doc:
Value-shaped twin of [`OKTSFFIError`].

`OKTSFFIError` is declared `#[derive(uniffi::Error)]` so it can be thrown
across the UniFFI boundary in `Result<T, OKTSFFIError>` returns. The
`uniffi::Error` derive emits `LowerError` / `LiftReturn` impls but **not**
the `FfiConverter` impl that record/state fields need — so the type cannot
also be stored in a `uniffi::Record`. Adding `uniffi::Enum` alongside
`uniffi::Error` would produce a conflicting `FfiConverter` impl.

`OKTSFFIErrorValue` mirrors the variants 1:1 but is derived only with
`uniffi::Enum`, making it usable as an `Option<_>` field on interactor
state. Interactor actions that need to surface the typed error to native
(currently recurring-buy pause/resume/stop — mirroring the place-order
`(error, error_code)` pair pattern) convert via `From<&OKTSFFIError>` at
the moment they assign the error into state.

store's own order.

Empty for a blank or non-recurring quote currency, and empty is also the
honest answer when the instrument store has nothing for this quote currency.
The caller treats empty as "no coins" and seeds nothing, which is what native
did with an empty filtered loop. A CANCELLED read is empty for the same
reason and with the same handling: cancellation here means the caller's page
setup was torn down, and seeding a basket for a page that is going away would
be worse than seeding nothing.

The order is the store's, which is the product's ranking. Callers must not
sort it.

The cancellation token is not optional decoration — UniFFI's built-in async
support cannot cancel, and this function awaits a network-backed load, so
without it a caller leaving the page would have no way to stop the work. The
repo enforces this: `scripts/check_async_uniffi_exports.sh` fails any
`#[uniffi::export] async fn` that neither takes a token nor uses the
`OKRustFuture` pattern.

doc:
Push the whole stored trade-config, all six fields.

Superset of [`set_price_settings`], which covers only the two ranges. The
other four (automatic tracking + its interval, pause tracking + its
threshold) are what [`save_trade_config`]'s blank-input fallback reads, so
a caller that fetches the config itself must push all six or a blank
interval will fall back to `0` instead of the stored value.

**Retirement trigger:** this exists because the iOS arm still fetches the
config through the legacy `OKTRequestCenter.getArbTradeConfig` in order to
hand an `OKTUserStrategyConfigModel` to the not-yet-twinned native content
tree. Once Wave C1 lands, iOS calls [`load_trade_config`] instead and this
setter has no consumer. Kept then only if Kotlin has adopted it.
